meta.notes: Category quotas exceed the floor targets in the brief. Primary intents sum to 200. Each candidate is real and documented. Avoid duplicates with founderDnaFounders.json pool.

candidates.name: Fred Rogers
candidates.rationale: Built a 33-year television practice rooted in treating children as whole people. His letters, scripts, and on-camera pauses form a disciplined pedagogy of patience and attunement that most nurturing-category people can recognize themselves in.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Maxwell King, The Good Neighbor (2018); Won't You Be My Neighbor? (2018 documentary); Fred Rogers Institute archive at Saint Vincent College; Rogers' 1969 Senate testimony transcript.

candidates.name: Maria Montessori
candidates.rationale: Developed an empirically grounded method for honoring children's self-directed development. Her own books document a precise craft of observing, preparing the environment, and withdrawing.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Montessori, The Absorbent Mind; Rita Kramer, Maria Montessori: A Biography (1976); AMI archives.

candidates.name: Anne Sullivan
candidates.rationale: Her letters to Sophia Hopkins describing the first weeks with Helen Keller are one of the clearest primary-source records of patient, adaptive teaching we have in English.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kim Nielsen, Beyond the Miracle Worker (2009); Anne Sullivan's letters published in Helen Keller's The Story of My Life.

candidates.name: Janusz Korczak
candidates.rationale: Ran a Warsaw orphanage on children's-rights principles decades before the UN codified them. Wrote How to Love a Child as a practitioner's manual.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Betty Jean Lifton, The King of Children (1988); Korczak, How to Love a Child and Ghetto Diary.

candidates.name: Vivian Gussin Paley
candidates.rationale: A kindergarten teacher who tape-recorded her classroom for decades and wrote twelve books of gentle, exacting analysis. MacArthur fellow for teaching as research.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Paley, The Boy Who Would Be a Helicopter and You Can't Say You Can't Play; New Yorker 2011 profile.

candidates.name: Jaime Escalante
candidates.rationale: Took East LA barrio students to AP Calculus mastery. His pedagogy of ganas is specific, documented, and radical.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Jay Mathews, Escalante: The Best Teacher in America (1988); Stand and Deliver making-of interviews.

candidates.name: Marva Collins
candidates.rationale: Founded Westside Preparatory in Chicago and taught reading to children the Chicago schools had given up on. Her Socratic method with 4-year-olds is documented in her own books.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Marva Collins' Way (1982); 60 Minutes profiles 1979 and 1995.

candidates.name: Rita Pierson
candidates.rationale: Forty years in classrooms distilled into the Every Kid Needs a Champion talk, which has become the de facto statement of the nurturing teacher's creed.
candidates.sourceStrategy: TED 2013 transcript; Pierson's teacher-training seminars archived by the Bluford Library.

candidates.name: James Stigler
candidates.rationale: Co-author of The Teaching Gap, built a career studying what excellent teachers actually do. His own papers are the first-person evidence.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Stigler and Hiebert, The Teaching Gap (1999); UCLA lab publications.

candidates.name: T. Berry Brazelton
candidates.rationale: Harvard pediatrician whose gentle, observational assessment of newborns reframed how a generation of parents thought about their babies.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Brazelton, Touchpoints; Boston Globe profiles; Brazelton Touchpoints Center archive.

candidates.name: Emmi Pikler
candidates.rationale: Ran Budapest's Loczy orphanage with an approach of respectful care and free movement that became an international reference.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Anna Tardos ed., Moving With Pleasure; Pikler-Loczy Institute archive.

candidates.name: Dan Hughes
candidates.rationale: Developed Dyadic Developmental Psychotherapy and wrote detailed clinical manuals on repairing attachment with traumatised children.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Hughes, Building the Bonds of Attachment; DDP Institute training papers.

candidates.name: Mary Ainsworth
candidates.rationale: Her Strange Situation experiments gave attachment theory its empirical spine. Her Uganda fieldwork is a rare first-person record of watching mothers and babies.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Ainsworth, Infancy in Uganda (1967); Inge Bretherton's biographical essays.

candidates.name: Donald Winnicott
candidates.rationale: His BBC radio talks to parents in the 1940s are some of the warmest practitioner writing in the field. Coined 'the good-enough mother'.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Winnicott, The Child, the Family and the Outside World; Adam Phillips, Winnicott (1988).

candidates.name: Paul Farmer
candidates.rationale: Co-founded Partners in Health but the skill signal is his house-call practice in rural Haiti and Rwanda, treating one patient at a time while building systems.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Tracy Kidder, Mountains Beyond Mountains (2003); Farmer, Pathologies of Power; PIH archives.

candidates.name: Virginia Apgar
candidates.rationale: Invented the Apgar Score, a 10-second assessment that saved millions of newborns. Embodies nurturing through a simple, disciplined act of attention.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Selma Calmes' historical papers; Atul Gawande's New Yorker piece on scoring.

candidates.name: Cicely Saunders
candidates.rationale: Founded the modern hospice movement at St Christopher's. Her clinical writing on 'total pain' is a first-person record of how to care for the dying.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Shirley du Boulay, Cicely Saunders (1984); Saunders' collected letters.

candidates.name: Irena Sendler
candidates.rationale: Smuggled 2,500 Jewish children out of the Warsaw Ghetto with a network of forgers, nurses, and nuns. Kept jars of their real names buried in a garden so families could reunite.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Anna Mieszkowska, Mother of the Children of the Holocaust; Yad Vashem testimony.

candidates.name: Tenzin Palmo
candidates.rationale: Spent 12 years in a Himalayan cave, then founded a nunnery to develop female practitioners. Long interviews give first-person nurturing detail.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Vicki Mackenzie, Cave in the Snow; Tenzin Palmo's Buddhist Society lectures.

candidates.name: Joyce Banda
candidates.rationale: Before becoming president, ran the National Association of Business Women, training rural Malawian women in microfinance with patient cohort methods.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Banda's memoir From Day One; BBC Africa long-form interviews 2012-2014.

candidates.name: Wangari Maathai
candidates.rationale: The Green Belt Movement she built trained rural Kenyan women to plant 30 million trees. Unbowed is a first-person account of the patient, one-village-at-a-time method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Maathai, Unbowed (2006); Nobel lecture 2004.

candidates.name: Pearl Kazin Bell
candidates.rationale: A legendary New Yorker fiction editor whose correspondence with writers reads as a case study in developing voice without overwriting.
candidates.sourceStrategy: New York Review of Books archive; Pearl Kazin papers at Columbia.

candidates.name: Gordon Lish
candidates.rationale: Edited Carver, DeLillo, and Amy Hempel. His own lectures on the craft of pushing a writer are recorded and transcribed.
candidates.sourceStrategy: The Lish Notes; Paris Review interview; Carol Sklenicka, Raymond Carver: A Writer's Life.

candidates.name: Phil Jackson
candidates.rationale: Coached 11 NBA championships using Zen and Lakota ideas. His books document the interior work of developing a team.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Jackson, Sacred Hoops and Eleven Rings; Jackson's extended interviews with Oprah's Super Soul Sunday.

candidates.name: Pat Summitt
candidates.rationale: Coached Tennessee for 38 seasons with a documented graduation rate of 100%. Her player development rituals are specific and well recorded.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Summitt, Sum It Up; Sally Jenkins' long-form profiles in Sports Illustrated.

candidates.name: John Wooden
candidates.rationale: Treated coaching as classroom teaching. His Pyramid of Success is one of the earliest first-person systematic nurturing frameworks from an American coach.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Wooden, Wooden on Leadership; Wooden's 2001 TED talk.

candidates.name: Herbert Kohl
candidates.rationale: Wrote 36 Children and I Won't Learn From You as first-person reflections on teaching kids the system had written off.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kohl, 36 Children; New York Review of Books teaching essays.

candidates.name: Rafe Esquith
candidates.rationale: Taught Hobart Boulevard fifth-graders Shakespeare for 30 years and wrote four practitioner books documenting his method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Esquith, Teach Like Your Hair's on Fire; Hobart Shakespeareans PBS documentary.

candidates.name: Erin Gruwell
candidates.rationale: The Freedom Writers Diary is a first-person document of using writing to reach Long Beach teens after the 1992 LA riots.
candidates.sourceStrategy: The Freedom Writers Diary; Freedom Writers Foundation interviews.

candidates.name: Sebastian Junger
candidates.rationale: Tribe and Restrepo show his long, patient work with Afghan-war infantrymen and the veteran community. Long-form interviews give skill signal.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Junger, Tribe; Restrepo (2010); Joe Rogan and Tim Ferriss long interviews.

candidates.name: Richard Feynman
candidates.rationale: His Lectures on Physics and Surely You're Joking are practitioner texts on how to make the hardest ideas obvious. The Feynman technique is the tradition's namesake.
candidates.sourceStrategy: The Feynman Lectures; Surely You're Joking; Caltech archive of Messenger lectures.

candidates.name: Carl Sagan
candidates.rationale: Cosmos is the template for making scale, time, and cosmology feel intimate. His books are first-person on the craft of the analogy.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Keay Davidson, Carl Sagan: A Life; Sagan, Demon-Haunted World; Cosmos (1980).

candidates.name: David Attenborough
candidates.rationale: Sixty years of making the natural world feel close without condescending. Life on Air is his own account of craft.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Attenborough, Life on Air; BBC archives; Guardian long-form interviews 2018-2022.

candidates.name: Jacob Bronowski
candidates.rationale: The Ascent of Man shows a mathematician walking the history of human knowledge with one clear example at a time. The Auschwitz pond scene is a clarifying masterclass.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Bronowski, The Ascent of Man (1973); BBC archive.

candidates.name: Hans Rosling
candidates.rationale: Turned global development statistics into something people could feel. Factfulness is a first-person method book.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Rosling, Factfulness (2018); Gapminder.org; TED talks 2006-2014.

candidates.name: Oliver Sacks
candidates.rationale: Every Sacks case study is a gentle translation of a rare neurological world into ordinary language, without flattening the person.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Sacks, On the Move (autobiography); The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat; Lawrence Weschler biography.

candidates.name: Mary Roach
candidates.rationale: Turns taboo or technical subjects into clean, funny prose. Long-form interviews discuss her research method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Roach, Stiff and Packing for Mars; WBUR and Longform Podcast interviews.

candidates.name: Atul Gawande
candidates.rationale: The Checklist Manifesto and Being Mortal take dense clinical material and make it humane and actionable for non-specialists.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Gawande, The Checklist Manifesto and Being Mortal; New Yorker archive.

candidates.name: Jerome Bruner
candidates.rationale: Framed scaffolding and narrative modes of thought in first-person teaching essays.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Bruner, The Process of Education and Actual Minds, Possible Worlds.

candidates.name: Neil deGrasse Tyson
candidates.rationale: StarTalk and his Hayden director work produced thousands of hours of on-record explanation and many interviews on the craft of the lay metaphor.
candidates.sourceStrategy: StarTalk podcast archive; Tyson, Astrophysics for People in a Hurry.

candidates.name: Steven Pinker
candidates.rationale: The Sense of Style is an entire book on how to write clearly about complicated things, drawn from his own practice.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Pinker, The Sense of Style; Harvard lectures.

candidates.name: Sal Khan
candidates.rationale: Khan Academy began with a cousin tutoring video and grew into a free curriculum used by tens of millions. His long-form interviews and book describe the explainer craft.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Khan, The One World Schoolhouse; TED 2011; Khan Academy archive.

candidates.name: Marcus du Sautoy
candidates.rationale: Simonyi Professor for the Public Understanding of Science at Oxford. His BBC work on primes and symmetry is a reference in mathematical explanation.
candidates.sourceStrategy: du Sautoy, The Music of the Primes; BBC Horizon episodes.

candidates.name: Randall Munroe
candidates.rationale: What If? and Thing Explainer are book-length experiments in reducing vocabulary to make physics tangible.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Munroe, Thing Explainer and What If?; xkcd archive.

candidates.name: Brian Cox
candidates.rationale: BBC Wonders series and Radio 4's Infinite Monkey Cage translate CERN-level physics into broadcast-friendly awe without losing the math.
candidates.sourceStrategy: BBC Wonders series; The Infinite Monkey Cage podcast archive.

candidates.name: Ruth Westheimer
candidates.rationale: Made a taboo subject speakable in plain words on national radio. Her interviews are a long record of turning shame into literacy.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Westheimer, All in a Lifetime; Ask Dr Ruth documentary (2019).

candidates.name: Henry Louis Gates Jr.
candidates.rationale: Finding Your Roots and his Signifying Monkey show him translating genealogy and literary theory for mass audiences.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Gates, Colored People; Finding Your Roots (PBS); New Yorker profiles.

candidates.name: Julia Child
candidates.rationale: Mastering the Art of French Cooking is an eight-year exercise in writing down every step a French home cook took for granted.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Child, My Life in France; Bob Spitz, Dearie (2012).

candidates.name: Jacques Pepin
candidates.rationale: His La Technique volumes and PBS series are practitioner explanations of knife grip, egg omelette, and other fundamentals.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Pepin, The Apprentice; La Technique; Pepin's KQED archive.

candidates.name: Samin Nosrat
candidates.rationale: Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat breaks cookery into four elements and reorganises the craft for beginners. A canonical clarifying work.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Nosrat, Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat; Netflix series; Home Cooking podcast.

candidates.name: Harold McGee
candidates.rationale: On Food and Cooking is the Rosetta stone between chemistry and the kitchen, written by a practitioner of patient footnoted prose.
candidates.sourceStrategy: McGee, On Food and Cooking; Curious Cook column.

candidates.name: Marcus Aurelius
candidates.rationale: Meditations is a first-person practice book of reducing philosophy to the size of a daily instruction.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Meditations (Hays translation); Pierre Hadot, The Inner Citadel.

candidates.name: Epictetus
candidates.rationale: The Discourses, recorded by Arrian, show a teacher stripping philosophy to usable steps for students.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Epictetus, Discourses and Enchiridion; A.A. Long, Epictetus: A Guide to Stoic Living.

candidates.name: Ha-Joon Chang
candidates.rationale: 23 Things They Don't Tell You About Capitalism reframes economics in lay terms without dumbing down.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Chang, Economics: The User's Guide; Guardian interviews; Cambridge lectures.

candidates.name: Tim Gowers
candidates.rationale: Fields medallist who runs the Polymath project and blogs at length about how a mathematician actually thinks.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Gowers's Weblog; Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction.

candidates.name: Eugenia Cheng
candidates.rationale: How to Bake Pi and The Art of Logic use cooking to teach abstract maths. Long BBC interviews on method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Cheng, How to Bake Pi; BBC and Numberphile interviews.

candidates.name: Matthew Walker
candidates.rationale: Why We Sleep is a clean lay translation of sleep research. His long-form podcast appearances are disciplined explainer craft.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Walker, Why We Sleep; Joe Rogan, Huberman Lab interviews.

candidates.name: Siddhartha Mukherjee
candidates.rationale: The Emperor of All Maladies is the reference for turning a medical field into narrative without flattening its science.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Mukherjee, The Emperor of All Maladies; Gene: An Intimate History.

candidates.name: Mary Beard
candidates.rationale: SPQR and her BBC documentaries make Roman history feel present and arguable. A study in how a specialist writes for the public.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Beard, SPQR; Mary Beard's Meet the Romans; TLS columns.

candidates.name: Trevor Noah
candidates.rationale: Born a Crime is a sharp translation of apartheid and mixed-race identity for a global audience. His long-form podcast is a second record.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Noah, Born a Crime; What Now? With Trevor Noah.

candidates.name: George Steiner
candidates.rationale: After Babel is a thousand-page argument for translation as the core human act. His own method book.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Steiner, After Babel and Errata: An Examined Life.

candidates.name: Edith Grossman
candidates.rationale: Why Translation Matters is a working translator's argument about how meaning moves between worlds.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Grossman, Why Translation Matters; Paris Review Art of Translation interview.

candidates.name: Gregory Rabassa
candidates.rationale: Translator of One Hundred Years of Solitude. His memoir If This Be Treason is a practitioner's synthesis craft manual.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Rabassa, If This Be Treason (2005).

candidates.name: Isaiah Berlin
candidates.rationale: The Hedgehog and the Fox and his Russian Thinkers essays are models of making sense of intellectual traditions across languages.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Berlin, The Hedgehog and the Fox; Michael Ignatieff, Isaiah Berlin: A Life.

candidates.name: Clifford Geertz
candidates.rationale: Thick Description gave a generation of anthropologists a way of weaving whole-picture field accounts.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Geertz, The Interpretation of Cultures; Available Light.

candidates.name: Bruno Latour
candidates.rationale: Actor-Network Theory is an attempt to hold humans, objects, and ideas together in one picture. His books are first-person method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Latour, We Have Never Been Modern; Reassembling the Social.

candidates.name: Donella Meadows
candidates.rationale: Thinking in Systems is the clearest practitioner text on whole-picture thinking. Her Dear Folks columns show the work in progress.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Meadows, Thinking in Systems; The Academy for Systems Change archive.

candidates.name: Fritjof Capra
candidates.rationale: The Tao of Physics and The Web of Life are long-form attempts to bridge sciences and wisdom traditions.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Capra, The Tao of Physics; Center for Ecoliteracy archive.

candidates.name: Iain McGilchrist
candidates.rationale: The Master and His Emissary argues a whole-civilisation thesis from hemispheric research. Extensive long-form interviews.
candidates.sourceStrategy: McGilchrist, The Master and His Emissary; Channel McGilchrist lectures.

candidates.name: Lynn Margulis
candidates.rationale: Proposed symbiogenesis against fierce opposition. Her work is a case study in holding a big picture until the field catches up.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Margulis and Sagan, Microcosmos; New York Academy oral history.

candidates.name: E.O. Wilson
candidates.rationale: Consilience and The Diversity of Life are deliberate attempts to stitch biology, social science, and humanities into a single frame.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Wilson, Consilience and Naturalist (autobiography).

candidates.name: Mary Catherine Bateson
candidates.rationale: Composing a Life develops a metaphor of improvisational weaving for whole-life integration. A writer-practitioner.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Bateson, Composing a Life; With a Daughter's Eye.

candidates.name: Joseph Campbell
candidates.rationale: Pulled a global body of myth into a single hero-story structure. The Power of Myth interviews are a long synthesis record.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Campbell, The Hero with a Thousand Faces; The Power of Myth (PBS, 1988).

candidates.name: Mircea Eliade
candidates.rationale: The Sacred and the Profane pulls cross-cultural religious patterns into a single framework, written in first-person analytic prose.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Eliade, The Sacred and the Profane; Autobiography.

candidates.name: Karen Armstrong
candidates.rationale: A History of God is a 4000-year synthesis of how Jewish, Christian, and Muslim ideas of the divine formed each other.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Armstrong, A History of God; Charter for Compassion archives; TED 2008.

candidates.name: Susan Sontag
candidates.rationale: Against Interpretation and On Photography pull together art, war, and media into singular arguments.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Sontag, Against Interpretation; Reborn: Journals 1947-1963.

candidates.name: Claude Lévi-Strauss
candidates.rationale: Tristes Tropiques is a first-person record of a mind building a structuralist framework out of fieldwork across continents.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Lévi-Strauss, Tristes Tropiques; The Savage Mind.

candidates.name: Robin Wall Kimmerer
candidates.rationale: Braiding Sweetgrass weaves Western botanical science with Potawatomi ways of knowing. A canonical non-business synthesis book.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kimmerer, Braiding Sweetgrass and Gathering Moss; On Being interview 2016.

candidates.name: David Bohm
candidates.rationale: Wholeness and the Implicate Order and On Dialogue attempt to unify physics and conversation under one picture of reality.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Bohm, Wholeness and the Implicate Order; On Dialogue.

candidates.name: Gregory Bateson
candidates.rationale: Steps to an Ecology of Mind is a first-person integration of biology, psychiatry, and cybernetics.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Bateson, Steps to an Ecology of Mind; Mind and Nature.

candidates.name: Frances Yates
candidates.rationale: The Art of Memory pulls together medieval memory palaces, Renaissance hermeticism, and early modern science in one structure.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Yates, The Art of Memory; Warburg Institute archive.

candidates.name: Jill Lepore
candidates.rationale: These Truths is a single-volume US history that deliberately connects technology, gender, politics, and media across centuries.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Lepore, These Truths; New Yorker essays.

candidates.name: Yuval Noah Harari
candidates.rationale: Sapiens and Homo Deus are big-picture stitches across biology, economy, and culture, written as practitioner synthesis.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Harari, Sapiens; long-form Economist interviews.

candidates.name: Svante Pääbo
candidates.rationale: Built an entire new field by connecting ancient DNA with evolutionary biology. Neanderthal Man is a first-person account of the work.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Pääbo, Neanderthal Man (2014); Nobel lecture 2022.

candidates.name: Michael Pollan
candidates.rationale: The Omnivore's Dilemma ties agriculture, ecology, and ethics together in one accessible arc.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Pollan, The Omnivore's Dilemma; How to Change Your Mind.

candidates.name: Rebecca Solnit
candidates.rationale: Wanderlust and A Field Guide to Getting Lost interleave walking, art, and geography in a way that treats essays as thinking across fields.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Solnit, Wanderlust; LitHub columns.

candidates.name: Timothy Snyder
candidates.rationale: Bloodlands compresses Nazi and Soviet violence into a single demographic picture across a contested geography.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Snyder, Bloodlands; On Tyranny; Yale Open Courses.

candidates.name: David Graeber
candidates.rationale: Debt: The First 5000 Years weaves ethnography, monetary history, and moral theory across continents.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Graeber, Debt; The Dawn of Everything (with Wengrow).

candidates.name: Elaine Pagels
candidates.rationale: The Gnostic Gospels reframed early Christian history by stitching suppressed texts back into the story.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Pagels, The Gnostic Gospels; Beyond Belief; Princeton lectures.

candidates.name: Zadie Smith
candidates.rationale: Feel Free and Changing My Mind show a novelist stitching philosophy, pop culture, and race theory into single essays.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Smith, Feel Free; Paris Review Art of Fiction interview.

candidates.name: Martha Nussbaum
candidates.rationale: The Capabilities Approach is her attempt to stitch economics, human rights, and Aristotelian ethics together as one framework.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Nussbaum, Creating Capabilities; Upheavals of Thought.

candidates.name: Jane Jacobs
candidates.rationale: Organised neighbourhoods against Robert Moses. Her craft of weaving residents, shop owners, and city officials into coalitions is documented in her own writing.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Jacobs, The Death and Life of Great American Cities; Robert Kanigel, Eyes on the Street.

candidates.name: Ella Baker
candidates.rationale: Behind SNCC and the SCLC. Her method of building leaderful groups rather than starring herself is a textbook case of the connecting play style.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Barbara Ransby, Ella Baker and the Black Freedom Movement (2003).

candidates.name: Dorothy Height
candidates.rationale: Led the National Council of Negro Women for four decades, convening coalitions that men-led civil rights groups could not.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Height, Open Wide the Freedom Gates; Library of Congress oral history.

candidates.name: Bayard Rustin
candidates.rationale: Engineered the 1963 March on Washington in two months by brokering between unions, churches, and civil rights groups.
candidates.sourceStrategy: John D'Emilio, Lost Prophet; Rustin papers.

candidates.name: Fannie Lou Hamer
candidates.rationale: Built the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party from sharecropper communities. Her speeches are a master class in calling a scattered group into one room.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kay Mills, This Little Light of Mine; SNCC archives.

candidates.name: Grace Lee Boggs
candidates.rationale: Detroit's radical connector across labour, Black power, and community movements. Her autobiography is a first-person account of the work.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Boggs, Living for Change; Grace Lee, American Revolutionary (documentary).

candidates.name: Saul Alinsky
candidates.rationale: Rules for Radicals and Reveille for Radicals are practitioner books on building coalitions in neighbourhoods that the rest of the country had written off.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Alinsky, Rules for Radicals; Sanford Horwitt biography.

candidates.name: Václav Havel
candidates.rationale: Charter 77 and the Velvet Revolution were coalition work. His essays describe the practice of building a parallel civic society.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Havel, The Power of the Powerless; Disturbing the Peace.

candidates.name: Lech Wałęsa
candidates.rationale: Pulled 10 million workers into Solidarity. His interviews describe the gate-meeting-by-gate-meeting craft of the work.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Wałęsa, The Struggle and the Triumph; Frontline interviews 1989.

candidates.name: Harriet Tubman
candidates.rationale: Ran a rescue network that required trust across enslaved people, Quakers, free Black abolitionists, and Union officers.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kate Larson, Bound for the Promised Land (2003).

candidates.name: Frederick Douglass
candidates.rationale: Wove the transatlantic abolitionist movement together as speaker, newspaperman, and diplomat.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Douglass, Narrative and Life and Times; David Blight, Frederick Douglass (2018).

candidates.name: Jane Addams
candidates.rationale: Hull House in Chicago was a connecting engine for immigrants, reformers, and university women. Her own books document the method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Addams, Twenty Years at Hull House; Louise Knight, Citizen.

candidates.name: Dorothy Day
candidates.rationale: Built a national network of houses of hospitality for the homeless, held together by personalism and a monthly newspaper.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Day, The Long Loneliness; Jim Forest, All Is Grace.

candidates.name: Myles Horton
candidates.rationale: Highlander Folk School trained Rosa Parks and hundreds of Southern organisers by convening people who needed to meet.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Horton, The Long Haul (autobiography); We Make the Road by Walking (with Paulo Freire).

candidates.name: Paulo Freire
candidates.rationale: Pedagogy of the Oppressed frames teaching as a dialogical practice of connecting peasant learners to their own knowledge.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Freire, Pedagogy of the Oppressed; Letters to Cristina.

candidates.name: Studs Terkel
candidates.rationale: Working and Hard Times show a lifetime of bridging between strangers by asking the next question with real patience.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Terkel, Working; Touch and Go (memoir); WFMT archive.

candidates.name: Krista Tippett
candidates.rationale: On Being is 20 years of careful, cross-tradition conversation. Her book Becoming Wise is a practitioner reflection on interviewing.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Tippett, Becoming Wise; On Being archive.

candidates.name: Jimmy Carter
candidates.rationale: Post-White House Carter Center work brokering elections and eradicating Guinea worm is a long record of patient bridge-building.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Jonathan Alter, His Very Best (2020); Carter Center annual reports.

candidates.name: Desmond Tutu
candidates.rationale: Chaired the TRC and built reconciliation practices that are now exported to post-conflict societies.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Tutu, No Future Without Forgiveness; John Allen biography.

candidates.name: John Hume
candidates.rationale: The back-channel between Sinn Féin and Dublin that enabled the Good Friday Agreement was largely his patient work.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Hume, A New Ireland; BBC long-form interviews; O'Brien's biography.

candidates.name: Martti Ahtisaari
candidates.rationale: Aceh, Kosovo, and Namibia peace processes. His CMI playbook is a working connector's method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Ahtisaari, CMI annual reports; Nobel lecture 2008.

candidates.name: Tawakkol Karman
candidates.rationale: Organised Yemen's 2011 tent city of protesters across tribal and religious lines. Nobel lecture and Al Jazeera interviews document the method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Nobel lecture 2011; Women Journalists Without Chains archive.

candidates.name: Nawal El Saadawi
candidates.rationale: Built a transnational Arab feminist network from a prison cell and a psychiatric practice.
candidates.sourceStrategy: El Saadawi, Memoirs from the Women's Prison; Walking Through Fire.

candidates.name: Tarana Burke
candidates.rationale: Me Too started as a patient cohort practice for Black girl survivors in Alabama before going global.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Burke, Unbound (2021); Longform Podcast.

candidates.name: Ta-Nehisi Coates
candidates.rationale: Between the World and Me is a bridge between personal grief and collective reckoning, and his long-form interviews discuss the craft of holding multiple readers at once.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Coates, Between the World and Me; Atlantic archive.

candidates.name: Toni Morrison
candidates.rationale: Nobel laureate whose editorial work at Random House also nurtured a generation of Black writers. First-person reflection in The Source of Self-Regard.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Morrison, The Source of Self-Regard; Paris Review Art of Fiction.

candidates.name: James Baldwin
candidates.rationale: His essays translate personal experience into public argument with more precision than almost any writer of the century.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Baldwin, Notes of a Native Son; The Fire Next Time; I Am Not Your Negro (2016).

candidates.name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
candidates.rationale: We Should All Be Feminists and the TED Danger of a Single Story are disciplined acts of voice that moved millions.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Adichie, Dear Ijeawele; TED archive; New Yorker profile.

candidates.name: Patti Smith
candidates.rationale: Just Kids and M Train are first-person practitioner books about turning life into language.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Smith, Just Kids; M Train; Louisiana Channel interview.

candidates.name: Seamus Heaney
candidates.rationale: Nobel laureate with published lectures (The Redress of Poetry) that show the poet reflecting on his craft.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Heaney, The Redress of Poetry; Stepping Stones: Interviews with Seamus Heaney.

candidates.name: Wisława Szymborska
candidates.rationale: Nobel laureate whose Letters to Poets column is a 30-year practitioner record of what good voice is.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Szymborska, Nonrequired Reading; Nobel lecture 1996.

candidates.name: Mahmoud Darwish
candidates.rationale: The national poet of Palestine whose work gave voice to a stateless identity across the Arab world.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Darwish, Memory for Forgetfulness; Guardian profiles; Institute for Palestine Studies archive.

candidates.name: Audre Lorde
candidates.rationale: Sister Outsider and The Cancer Journals are among the clearest examples of turning lived experience into public voice.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Lorde, Sister Outsider; Alexis de Veaux, Warrior Poet.

candidates.name: Nina Simone
candidates.rationale: Mississippi Goddam and her Montreux sets are the expressing category in its purest, most politicised form.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Simone, I Put a Spell on You; What Happened, Miss Simone? (2015).

candidates.name: Mercedes Sosa
candidates.rationale: The Voice of Latin America. Her performances during and after exile unified a continent around a set of songs.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Sosa, La Negra; documentary Mercedes Sosa: La Voz de Latinoamérica (2013).

candidates.name: Fela Kuti
candidates.rationale: Invented Afrobeat and used it as a public address system against the Nigerian military government.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Carlos Moore, Fela: This Bitch of a Life; Finding Fela (Alex Gibney documentary).

candidates.name: Miriam Makeba
candidates.rationale: Brought South African music to the UN and to the world while in exile.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Makeba, My Story; Mama Africa (2011 documentary).

candidates.name: Aretha Franklin
candidates.rationale: Her vocal craft and Amazing Grace sessions are reference points for the expressing category at its highest technical level.
candidates.sourceStrategy: David Ritz, Respect: The Life of Aretha Franklin; Amazing Grace (2018 film).

candidates.name: Luciano Pavarotti
candidates.rationale: Pulled opera into stadiums and football through Nessun Dorma. His masterclasses are first-person craft records.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Pavarotti, My World; Pavarotti (2019 Ron Howard documentary).

candidates.name: Maya Angelou
candidates.rationale: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings and her Presidential inaugural poem are canonical acts of voice.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Angelou, I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings; Iconoclasts interview.

candidates.name: Tupac Shakur
candidates.rationale: Interviews and poetry show a rapper with a deliberate sense of his own voice as a form of political and personal speech.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Tupac, The Rose That Grew from Concrete; Resurrection (2003).

candidates.name: Lin-Manuel Miranda
candidates.rationale: Hamilton is an extended exercise in putting marginalised history into a dominant form. Long-form interviews describe craft.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Miranda, Hamilton: The Revolution; Longform Podcast.

candidates.name: Ira Glass
candidates.rationale: This American Life's 30-year method is the de facto textbook for narrative radio. His taste-gap talk is a craft reference.
candidates.sourceStrategy: This American Life archive; The Believer interview.

candidates.name: Shakespeare
candidates.rationale: The closest thing English has to a north star for the expressing category. Language itself reshaped by one writer's voice.
candidates.sourceStrategy: The Norton Shakespeare; James Shapiro, 1599 and Contested Will.

candidates.name: Rumi
candidates.rationale: The Masnavi is seven hundred years of continuous influence on how people speak of love and the divine.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Coleman Barks translations; Franklin Lewis, Rumi: Past and Present, East and West.

candidates.name: Kae Tempest
candidates.rationale: Let Them Eat Chaos and On Connection are first-person on the craft of performing voice without losing precision.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Tempest, On Connection; Louisiana Channel interview.

candidates.name: Wong Kar-wai
candidates.rationale: In the Mood for Love is an entire film as one sustained act of emotional voice. His commentary tracks document the craft.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Criterion Collection commentaries; Film Comment long-form interview.

candidates.name: Frida Kahlo
candidates.rationale: Her diaries and letters are a first-person record of making something that did not exist before out of pain and cultural material.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Hayden Herrera, Frida: A Biography; The Diary of Frida Kahlo.

candidates.name: Hilma af Klint
candidates.rationale: Invented abstraction before Kandinsky and hid the work for 20 years. A case study in creating outside market logic.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Julia Voss, Hilma af Klint; Guggenheim 2018 catalogue.

candidates.name: Louise Bourgeois
candidates.rationale: Her Insomnia Drawings and diaries are a first-person record of making over 60 years.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Bourgeois, Destruction of the Father / Reconstruction of the Father; Deborah Wye, Louise Bourgeois.

candidates.name: Ursula K. Le Guin
candidates.rationale: Steering the Craft and Dancing at the Edge of the World are craft books by a working writer.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Le Guin, Steering the Craft; Paris Review Art of Fiction.

candidates.name: Haruki Murakami
candidates.rationale: What I Talk About When I Talk About Running and Novelist as a Vocation are first-person books about the routine of making fiction.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Murakami, Novelist as a Vocation; What I Talk About When I Talk About Running.

candidates.name: Octavia Butler
candidates.rationale: Her journals at the Huntington Library are a documented record of a Black woman writer willing herself into the genre.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Huntington Butler archive; Lynell George, A Handful of Earth, A Handful of Sky.

candidates.name: Hayao Miyazaki
candidates.rationale: The Kingdom of Dreams and Madness documentary and his Starting Point essays show a practitioner describing his process.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Miyazaki, Starting Point 1979-1996; The Kingdom of Dreams and Madness (2013).

candidates.name: Akira Kurosawa
candidates.rationale: Something Like an Autobiography is a clear first-person account of inventing a visual language for Japanese film.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kurosawa, Something Like an Autobiography; Stuart Galbraith IV, The Emperor and the Wolf.

candidates.name: Gabriel García Márquez
candidates.rationale: Living to Tell the Tale is his own account of making One Hundred Years of Solitude out of memory and reporting.
candidates.sourceStrategy: García Márquez, Living to Tell the Tale; Paris Review Art of Fiction.

candidates.name: Toni Cade Bambara
candidates.rationale: The Writer's Situation interviews show an artist talking about making work that did not exist for Black women writers before.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Bambara, Deep Sightings and Rescue Missions; Toni Cade Bambara: What It Is I Think I'm Doing Anyhow.

candidates.name: Georgia O'Keeffe
candidates.rationale: Her published writings and letters are first-person on inventing a visual vocabulary for American landscape and flower.
candidates.sourceStrategy: O'Keeffe, Some Memories of Drawings; Roxana Robinson biography.

candidates.name: Yayoi Kusama
candidates.rationale: Infinity Net is an autobiography of a lifelong compulsion to make. A paradigm case of creating as survival.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kusama, Infinity Net; Louisiana Channel interview.

candidates.name: Philip Glass
candidates.rationale: Words Without Music is his first-person memoir of inventing a style through practice.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Glass, Words Without Music.

candidates.name: Björk
candidates.rationale: Continuously reinvents album formats, instruments, and collaborations. Her long-form interviews describe the inventive logic.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Björk, Biophilia educational materials; Pitchfork 50th Q&A.

candidates.name: Anni Albers
candidates.rationale: On Weaving and On Designing are working books by a Bauhaus practitioner inventing a field.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Albers, On Weaving; Tate 2018 catalogue.

candidates.name: Chinua Achebe
candidates.rationale: Things Fall Apart invented a register of English for African storytelling. His essays explain the choice.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Achebe, Morning Yet on Creation Day; There Was a Country.

candidates.name: Clarice Lispector
candidates.rationale: Invented a style of Portuguese prose that had no precedent. Her chronicles show the method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Benjamin Moser, Why This World: A Biography of Clarice Lispector.

candidates.name: Antoni Gaudí
candidates.rationale: Sagrada Família is the reference for creating a new architectural vocabulary out of nature and Catholicism.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Gijs van Hensbergen, Gaudí: A Biography; Sagrada Família archive.

candidates.name: William Kentridge
candidates.rationale: Six Drawing Lessons is his own Harvard series on how his work is made. A clean practitioner record.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kentridge, Six Drawing Lessons; Louisiana Channel interviews.

candidates.name: Andrei Tarkovsky
candidates.rationale: Sculpting in Time is a director's book on inventing a film language out of duration and memory.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Tarkovsky, Sculpting in Time; Martyrolog (diaries).

candidates.name: Marcel Duchamp
candidates.rationale: Pierre Cabanne's Dialogues are a rare book-length interview with the inventor of conceptual art.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Cabanne, Dialogues with Marcel Duchamp; Calvin Tomkins biography.

candidates.name: Dieter Rams
candidates.rationale: Ten Principles of Good Design is the canonical practitioner framework. His Rams documentary shows working method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Rams, Ten Principles; Rams (Gary Hustwit, 2018).

candidates.name: Charles and Ray Eames
candidates.rationale: Powers of Ten and the Lounge Chair are two of the cleanest examples of designing both experience and function.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Pat Kirkham, Charles and Ray Eames; Eames Office archive.

candidates.name: Massimo Vignelli
candidates.rationale: Designed the NYC subway map and American Airlines identity. His Canon is a first-person design manifesto.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Vignelli, The Vignelli Canon (free PDF); Design Is One documentary.

candidates.name: Tadao Ando
candidates.rationale: Concrete, light and silence as a designed experience. His interviews with the Louisiana Museum are a practitioner's method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Ando, Tadao Ando: Conversations with Students; Louisiana Channel.

candidates.name: Paula Scher
candidates.rationale: Pentagram partner whose work for the Public Theater and Citibank is in design canon. Abstract: The Art of Design episode documents process.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Scher, Make It Bigger; Abstract S1E6.

candidates.name: Zaha Hadid
candidates.rationale: Pritzker laureate who redefined how buildings can feel. Long-form profiles document the design method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Philip Jodidio, Hadid: Complete Works; Guardian profiles.

candidates.name: Kenya Hara
candidates.rationale: Designing Design is a first-person book by the Muji art director on emptiness as a design principle.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Hara, Designing Design and White.

candidates.name: Kevin Lynch
candidates.rationale: The Image of the City invented the language of legibility and mental maps, from his own fieldwork method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Lynch, The Image of the City.

candidates.name: Jan Gehl
candidates.rationale: Cities for People is a 40-year record of designing streets around how human bodies actually behave.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Gehl, Cities for People; Gehl Architects studies.

candidates.name: Achille Castiglioni
candidates.rationale: His teaching notes and lectures at Milan Polytechnic are a first-person archive of play as design method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Studio Castiglioni archive; Achille Castiglioni: Complete Works.

candidates.name: Gertrude Jekyll
candidates.rationale: Invented the herbaceous border and wrote 15 practitioner books on how to design a garden as sequence and colour.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Jekyll, Colour in the Flower Garden; Sally Festing biography.

candidates.name: Piet Oudolf
candidates.rationale: Designed the High Line's plantings. Five Seasons documentary and long interviews describe his way of designing for decay.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Five Seasons: The Gardens of Piet Oudolf (2017); Planting: A New Perspective.

candidates.name: Malcolm X
candidates.rationale: The autobiography and speeches are a first-person record of moving a community from acquiescence to action.
candidates.sourceStrategy: The Autobiography of Malcolm X; Manning Marable, Malcolm X: A Life of Reinvention.

candidates.name: Mahatma Gandhi
candidates.rationale: His autobiography is a first-person account of how to move a nation by small, disciplined acts.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Gandhi, An Autobiography: The Story of My Experiments with Truth; Ramachandra Guha biographies.

candidates.name: Gloria Steinem
candidates.rationale: Fifty years of talking circles, speeches, and journalism that moved the American conversation about women and work.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Steinem, My Life on the Road; Outrageous Acts and Everyday Rebellions.

candidates.name: Malala Yousafzai
candidates.rationale: Nobel laureate whose UN speech and book turned a Pakistani teenager into a global advocacy voice.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Yousafzai, I Am Malala; Malala Fund reports.

candidates.name: Greta Thunberg
candidates.rationale: How Dare You and the school strikes are a measurable influence event. Long-form Guardian and Time interviews show method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Thunberg, No One Is Too Small to Make a Difference; I Am Greta (2020).

candidates.name: Al Gore
candidates.rationale: An Inconvenient Truth and the Climate Reality trainings are a 20-year record of one man trying to move public opinion.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Gore, An Inconvenient Truth; Climate Reality Project archive.

candidates.name: Marshall Ganz
candidates.rationale: Framed the story-of-self/story-of-us/story-of-now method used by Obama 2008 and climate groups. His Harvard teaching materials are first-person.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Ganz, Why David Sometimes Wins; Harvard Kennedy School course packs.

candidates.name: Cesar Chavez
candidates.rationale: The UFW grape boycott moved supermarket buyers and families across America through patient house meetings.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Miriam Pawel, The Crusades of Cesar Chavez; UFW archives.

candidates.name: Dolores Huerta
candidates.rationale: Co-founded the UFW and coined Sí, se puede. Dolores (2017) is a long-form record of her craft.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Dolores (2017 documentary); Huerta, Dolores Huerta: Revolution in the Fields.

candidates.name: Marshall McLuhan
candidates.rationale: The medium is the message reshaped how a generation of communicators thought about moving people. His own books are first-person method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: McLuhan, Understanding Media and The Medium Is the Massage.

candidates.name: Naomi Klein
candidates.rationale: No Logo and The Shock Doctrine moved global debates about capitalism. Long interviews describe her reporting method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Klein, No Logo; This Changes Everything.

candidates.name: Marie Curie
candidates.rationale: Her lab notebooks and Eve Curie's biography are a first-person record of refusing to stop until the numbers made sense.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Eve Curie, Madame Curie; Curie's Nobel lectures.

candidates.name: Rosalind Franklin
candidates.rationale: Photograph 51 and her coal studies are a case study in rigorous pattern extraction from noisy data.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Brenda Maddox, Rosalind Franklin: The Dark Lady of DNA.

candidates.name: Barbara McClintock
candidates.rationale: Discovered jumping genes decades before the field accepted them. Her Feeling for the Organism biography documents the watching craft.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Evelyn Fox Keller, A Feeling for the Organism.

candidates.name: Katherine Johnson
candidates.rationale: NASA 'human computer' whose hand calculations John Glenn trusted over the IBMs. Her own NASA oral history is first-person.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Margot Lee Shetterly, Hidden Figures; NASA oral history.

candidates.name: Jane Goodall
candidates.rationale: Sixty years of patient observation that changed how a field saw chimpanzees. Her books and the NatGeo field notes are primary source.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Goodall, In the Shadow of Man; Reason for Hope; Jane (2017).

candidates.name: Rachel Carson
candidates.rationale: Silent Spring is a compiled investigation of DDT evidence that the US government had been ignoring. She trained as a biologist first.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Linda Lear, Rachel Carson: Witness for Nature.

candidates.name: Aldo Leopold
candidates.rationale: A Sand County Almanac is phenological fieldwork written in public-facing prose. Thinking like a mountain is his.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Leopold, A Sand County Almanac; Curt Meine biography.

candidates.name: Cedric Villani
candidates.rationale: Fields medallist whose Birth of a Theorem is a first-person diary of the analytic craft on optimal transport.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Villani, Birth of a Theorem; Collège de France lectures.

candidates.name: Anna Politkovskaya
candidates.rationale: Her Chechnya reporting is a model of patient, dangerous pattern extraction from a conflict most reporters did not touch.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Politkovskaya, A Small Corner of Hell; A Russian Diary.

candidates.name: Susan Fowler
candidates.rationale: Whistleblower is a first-person account of documenting harassment at Uber with the precision of an engineer.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Fowler, Whistleblower; New York Times tech interviews.

candidates.name: Cathy O'Neil
candidates.rationale: Weapons of Math Destruction is a practitioner account of auditing algorithms for social harm.
candidates.sourceStrategy: O'Neil, Weapons of Math Destruction; mathbabe.org archive.

candidates.name: Viktor Frankl
candidates.rationale: Man's Search for Meaning is a first-person argument for strategy as choosing an orientation under any conditions. His logotherapy is method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Frankl, Man's Search for Meaning; Yes to Life In Spite of Everything.

candidates.name: George Kennan
candidates.rationale: Long Telegram is a case study in seeing the whole board 20 years ahead. His Memoirs are first-person.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Kennan, Memoirs 1925-1950; John Lewis Gaddis, George F. Kennan: An American Life.

candidates.name: Carl von Clausewitz
candidates.rationale: On War is the founding practitioner text of strategic thinking in the Western tradition.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Clausewitz, On War; Peter Paret biography.

candidates.name: Frank Lloyd Wright
candidates.rationale: Designed and constructed over 500 buildings across seven decades, defining organic architecture through the Prairie and Usonian houses. His autobiography is a working architect's account of turning ideas into structures.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Wright, An Autobiography; Ada Louise Huxtable, Frank Lloyd Wright; Taliesin Foundation archives.

candidates.name: Hedy Lamarr
candidates.rationale: Co-invented frequency-hopping spread-spectrum. Bombshell documentary uses her own tapes as first-person material.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Richard Rhodes, Hedy's Folly; Bombshell (2017).

candidates.name: Florence Nightingale
candidates.rationale: Turned British military hospitals from chaos into running systems, largely through her statistical work and her Notes on Nursing.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Nightingale, Notes on Nursing; Mark Bostridge, Florence Nightingale.

candidates.name: Clara Barton
candidates.rationale: Built the American Red Cross out of battlefield improvisation. Her letters and Stephen Oates biography show the method.
candidates.sourceStrategy: Stephen Oates, A Woman of Valor; American Red Cross archives.
